method.summary: Every .mov was decoded to individual frames and read as images. Contact sheets and keyframes were opened as well, but they were not the primary source: the packet's own keyframe sets sample video C at 4-second intervals, which is coarser than several of the transitions this concept had to reproduce.
method.decoder: ffmpeg 7.0.2-static (H.264/avc1). No ffmpeg or ffprobe is installed on this machine; the bundled Playwright ffmpeg has no H.264 decoder at all, so a static build already present on disk was used.
review_passes: Indexed contact sheets at a known stride, so any cell maps back to an exact frame number.
Native-rate micro-sheets across each transition, cropped to the region that moves.
Upscaled single frames where the source resolution made the copy unreadable.
method.limitations: No audio was reviewed; none of the four recordings carries information in its audio track. Frame indices below are 1-based and refer to the full-rate decode.

what_it_established: The activity stream is ONE evolving capsule, not a growing list of tool rows.
Each finished phase leaves exactly one glyph behind: two by f.208, three by f.390, four by f.780, six by f.910.
The glyph chain is a RANDOM-ACCESS INDEX. After the run condenses, clicking the pencil at f.1170 reopens 'Made 1 create, 2 edits' and clicking the magnifier at f.1300 reopens 'Explored 7 files'.
The count is rewritten IN PLACE: 'Exploring 5 files' to '6 files' to '7 files' across f.208, f.286 and f.338, on the same row at the same y, with no relayout.
The verb changes tense on settle: Thinking/Exploring/Making while running, Thought/Explored/Made once finished.
A phase hands over in TWO BEATS, f.194 to f.211 (about 0.44s): the label cross-fades first, and only then does the new glyph open its slot and push the label right by exactly one slot.

Condense is the RESTING STATE, not a deletion. At f.910 the run becomes '13 tools used'; the prose answer, the verification row and the artifact card sit below it and are pushed down when a phase is reopened.
The chain rolls rather than truncating once it exceeds roughly six glyphs, and scrolls a selected glyph back into view.
Sub-row grammar is bold verb plus muted argument, hung off a left hairline rule, with the diff stat right-aligned as +n green / -n crimson.
The artifact card resolves in place from 'Compiling...' to 'Version 1.2', and a footer meta line reads 'Worked for 1m 34s'.

what_it_established: The card LOOKS stable across pages — but the second reading found why, and it matters: every one of its four pages carries exactly FOUR option rows. The stability is a property of the content, not a reserved frame. A concept whose pages genuinely differ (single select, multi select, freeform textarea) cannot copy it; it would have to engineer a reservation the reference never demonstrates.
Paging backwards is a first-class action and the load-bearing half: at 11.00s and 19.80s it returns to '1 of 4' with the typed answer still present, and both chevrons stay live throughout.
The header pager reads '1 of 4' with prev/next chevrons and a close control; hovering the forward chevron shows a 'Next' tooltip.
Options are numbered chips plus muted text; the LAST row is a freeform capsule whose inline pill button reads 'Skip' when empty and 'Next' once text is typed.
The composer stays live below the card, placeholdered 'Or reply directly...' - the question never locks it.
On the final page 'Skip' is replaced by a 'Submit' pill rendered disabled until an option is chosen.

The card RESIZES rather than holding a frame. Backward paging is measured: tools/drive.mjs paging records, per concept, root identity, whether the entrance replayed, and whether the answer is still shown.

defects_found_while_reviewing.summary: Operation rows printed a line delta for operations that have none.
defects_found_while_reviewing.evidence: Two renderers concatenated +r.added and -r.removed unguarded; two more defaulted them with || 0.
defects_found_while_reviewing.consequence: Once the corpus gained sub-rows for reads, searches, fetches, browser opens and checks - none of which touch lines - the unguarded pair rendered the literal '+undefined -undefined', and the defaulted pair rendered '+0 -0', which asserts a zero-line edit that did not happen either.
defects_found_while_reviewing.fixed: All four now omit the delta when absent. Two of the concepts already carried the correct guard a few hundred lines away in the same file, which is what a shared record and eight independent renderings costs when the record grows a new shape.

defects_found_while_reviewing.summary: `[data-motion="full"] *` reverted animation-duration to 0s, killing every class-driven animation inside an explicitly-full stage.
defects_found_while_reviewing.evidence: The rule matched at (0,1,0) — the same specificity as every animation class in motion.css — and came later in the file, so `revert-layer` rolled the duration back to the user-agent default. Measured: inside the stage `animation-name: pmx-size-bounce-strong` with `animation-duration: 0s`; the identical element outside the stage reported 0.42s.
defects_found_while_reviewing.consequence: Not one class-driven animation ran inside a full stage: not .pmx-enter, not .pmx-cascade, not any of the thirteen families, not the new resize bounce. The rule could not even achieve its stated purpose, because the reduced-motion blanket it was trying to undo is `!important` and `revert-layer` is not. The third instance of this exact failure signature in one file.
defects_found_while_reviewing.fixed: The OS-preference blanket now excludes an explicitly-full stage at the source, and the revert-layer rule is gone. A rule that never applies needs no counter-rule. Verified: full stage 0.42s / 0.26s, reduced stage 0s / 1e-05s.

defects_found_while_reviewing.summary: Every morphed count digit came to rest 4px low at 45% opacity.

defects_found_while_reviewing.consequence: The digit never visibly settled in any concept that morphs a count — measured in t1, t2 and t5. Behaviour 2 of the activity reference reached the screen parked on its own first frame.
defects_found_while_reviewing.fixed: The run state now out-specifies the start state, and endNow clears the direction attribute so the resting state is neutral whatever the cascade does. Verified resolved: opacity 1, transform none, in both directions.

defects_found_while_reviewing.summary: The automated matrix swept no themes at all, ran two of the four canon widths, and never asserted focus — against a packet line that names all three.
defects_found_while_reviewing.found_by: Reading CORRECTION_GOAL_PROMPT.md's last required-proof line against the harness rather than against the documentation.
defects_found_while_reviewing.detail: CORRECTION_GOAL_PROMPT.md requires that “all themes, widths, reduced motion, keyboard/focus, long content, errors, reconnect idempotency, and non-showcase pairings pass”. Measured against the suite: `theme` and `ui.theme` appeared ZERO times in tests/suites.js, so eight themes were offered, selectable and documented as covered while nothing asserted that any of them rendered. The width sweep ran 520 and 750, so the two widths at which the artifact workspace and pinned history actually coexist — exactly where a layout runs out of room — were never swept. And `activeElement` appeared zero times, while shared/motion.js states as its rule 3 that “not one helper touches focus”: a docblock, not a check. This is the report-versus-measurement failure this workspace keeps producing, committed against the packet's own acceptance line.
defects_found_while_reviewing.fix: The matrix now sweeps all four canon widths and adds a theme axis — 8 themes x 4 widths on the two structural extremes, as its own axis rather than multiplied through 64 pairings, which would be 2,048 runs to re-prove the same tokens sixty-four times. A new `focus` suite asserts that a full activity run and a question opening leave focus on the composer in all eight thread concepts. COVERAGE.md's stale claims are corrected at the top of the file rather than edited into the tables.

defects_found_while_reviewing.summary: Nine of the ten command ids an operation card prints were absent from candidate-command-delta.json, and three delta rows claimed “new” on evidence the catalog contradicts.
defects_found_while_reviewing.found_by: Extracting every cmd.* id from source and from the wiring delta and diffing both against the command delta, then re-checking each remaining “new” against the 540 canonical table rows in Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md.
defects_found_while_reviewing.detail: shared/opcard.js states in its own docblock that “every id minted here is also recorded in candidate-command-delta.json for the owner to accept, rename or reject”. Nine of its ten were not, so a card printed a COMMAND row the catalog owner had never been shown. Checking them against the catalog then found three that must not be minted at all: `cmd.chat.web.search` is already canonical, `cmd.browser.navigate` already owns driving a page, and `cmd.testing.run` already owns running a suite. A second sweep over the existing rows found three more dispositioned “new” on false evidence — the worst being `cmd.chat.bsd.set`, recorded as new because “no cmd.bsd.* or Back Seat Driver id exists anywhere in the catalog” when `cmd.bsd.set` is canonical at :11109 with the concept's own Off/Auto/On enum and Auto default — and three ids that lived only in candidate-wiring-delta.json and had therefore never been put in front of the file whose job is to check them.
defects_found_while_reviewing.fix: opcard.js now emits the canonical ids. The delta carries all 48 rows with corrected dispositions, and `node tools/drive.mjs scan` fails on any cmd.* id in surface source or in the wiring delta that the command delta does not record — 44 ids checked, 0 unrecorded. An unknown stage kind no longer builds `cmd.chat.activity.<kind>` on the spot, which was a mint no source grep could ever see.

defects_found_while_reviewing.summary: The widened matrix took one Chromium to 12.8 GB and the host fully into swap.
defects_found_while_reviewing.found_by: Watching host memory while the widened sweep ran, after the user had already had to restart this machine once for running out of RAM.
defects_found_while_reviewing.detail: runMatrix chained its runs with plain `.then()`. A promise chain of synchronous mounts is one unbroken block of work — microtasks drain before the event loop gets a turn — so the browser never painted, never ran a full GC, and never let the driver read progress, while every mounted composition stayed reachable from the accumulating result until the whole sweep resolved. Heap therefore grew with the TOTAL number of runs rather than with the widest one. At 128 runs that was survivable; widening to 320 was not. This was introduced by the REF-17 fix, which is the point worth keeping: closing a coverage gap made the harness unrunnable, and only watching the host caught it.
defects_found_while_reviewing.fix: The sweep yields to the macrotask queue between runs so GC and paint can happen at all, and the driver runs it in chunks — one per window plus one for the theme axis — each in a freshly navigated page, which discards each chunk's heap outright and bounds the sweep at one window's worth however wide the matrix later becomes.

defects_found_while_reviewing.detail: CORRECTION_GOAL_PROMPT.md requires “Update interaction, visual, demo-trigger, Plan-owner, candidate Command/Wiring/DRY, and known-gap reports.” Six of the seven were updated during the correction; the Plan-owner delta was not touched at all, so the run-trace contract, the resize primitive and the attachment family had no Plan-impact statement.

defects_found_while_reviewing.summary: Activating an activity chain glyph with the keyboard dropped focus to <body> in all eight thread concepts.
defects_found_while_reviewing.found_by: Writing the focus assertion the packet's acceptance line implies, then running it with the fix disabled to check it could fail.
defects_found_while_reviewing.detail: Seven of the eight concepts rebuild their activity capsule when the phase kind changes, so the glyph a reader has focused is destroyed and replaced by an equal-looking new element mid-interaction. Focus then falls back to <body>, which for a keyboard reader means being returned to the top of the document by their own click. `activeElement` appeared nowhere in shared/, threads/ or windows/, so nothing anywhere was preserving it. Measured with the fix disabled: 8 of 8 fail. A weaker assertion — that a focusable control still EXISTS after the render — passes in all eight while focus is on <body>, which is why the check is written as a position match instead.
defects_found_while_reviewing.fix: PMXUtil.keepFocusAcross(root, mutateFn) records the focused element's position path within root, runs the mutation, and re-focuses whatever now stands at that path — with preventScroll, so it cannot undo ScrollCtl.preserveAcross — and ONLY when focus was actually dropped, so a concept that deliberately moves focus is not fought. It is wired at Composition._onState, the single point every store-driven re-render passes through, rather than in eight concepts: a concept can only protect the renders it knows it caused, and focus is lost by whichever render happens to land. It is deliberately NOT in shared/motion.js, whose third rule is that no motion helper touches focus.

defects_found_while_reviewing.summary: Behaviour 4 of 03_compact_execution_activity.mov was asserted at the record level only, never geometrically.
defects_found_while_reviewing.found_by: Walking the five behaviours shared/runtrace.js cites by frame index and asking, for each, which assertion holds it.
defects_found_while_reviewing.detail: f.910: the run condenses to one summary row, and the prose answer, the verification row and the artifact card live BELOW it and are pushed down when a phase is reopened, never replaced. What existed was `every work surface is still live after a condense` — true of the record, silent about the screen. A capsule that overlays what is beneath it, and one that swaps its region's contents, both leave that assertion passing and the reading ruined.
defects_found_while_reviewing.fix: The suite now measures the y of the content below the capsule across a reopen, in all eight concepts. Written first as an element-identity check it failed in seven — and that was the CHECK being wrong: seven rebuild the region, and a viewer cannot see element identity. Rewritten to compare content and position, which is what the recording can actually show, it passes in eight. Checked for teeth by running it with a strict must-move instead of must-not-move-up: six of the eight still pass, so the displacement is real and the looser form is a guard rather than a vacuum.

defects_found_while_reviewing.summary: TEST_REPORT.md reported two documented design differences as failures, and printed three measured columns as “n/a”.
defects_found_while_reviewing.found_by: Reading the generated report rather than the JSON it was generated from.
defects_found_while_reviewing.detail: The activity probe deliberately keeps three dimensions OUT of its exit gate, with the reasoning written at the gate. The report generator did not know that, so it collected every false in every verdict and printed “Concepts with a failing verdict: t2, t8” directly beneath a table it had just filled from a run that exited 0. A file whose premise is that it never states anything the measurement did not say was contradicting the measurement's own exit code. Separately, its cell formatter rendered anything that was not a boolean or a number as “n/a”, so `sentence row via` and `handover beats` — both measured, both useful — printed as three columns of the word “n/a”.
defects_found_while_reviewing.fix: drive.mjs now emits `gatedVerdictKeys` and `recordedVerdictKeys` (the latter carrying the reason each dimension is recorded rather than failed), and report.mjs reads them instead of deciding for itself — so the summary cannot drift from the exit code. Gated columns are bold in the table, and arrays and strings now print as themselves.

still_open.summary: The question card now resizes with this product’s own tuned bounce, in all eight concepts.
still_open.detail: The stable-frame reading was withdrawn on instruction. The reference’s card only LOOKS stable because every one of its pages carries exactly four option rows; our pages genuinely differ (single select, multi select, freeform), so stability would have had to be engineered rather than observed. Instead the card bounces, reproducing PMConcept7’s model-picker resize: height on cubic-bezier(.22,1.72,.36,1) so it overshoots and settles, plus a restarted scale beat, measured start, height:auto remeasure so max-height is respected, and a sub-pixel bail. Six concepts carried written refusals of height motion; all six were rewritten rather than left contradicting the code, and `pmx-resize-up` answers most of what they were protecting by moving the card’s own top edge instead of the content below it.

still_open.summary: The two-beat handover now plays in all eight concepts; the lateral push plays where the geometry supports it.
still_open.detail: Measured `handoverClearsBeforeNewGlyph` true for 8/8. t2, t4, t5, t6 and t7 drive it through motion.phaseHandover; t1, t3 and t8 express the same two beats in their own geometry, because their chains sit where a lateral slot-opening would either reach nothing or push the wrong element. t4 was converted to identity-preserving chain reconciliation on the t2 pattern, which is what its own comment had been asking for.

still_open.summary: The headline read-back failure was two unrelated causes; both are settled.
still_open.detail: t2 was a fault in the probe: it derived "the header" as the parent of the first run-verb, and t2 has no header row at all — its sentence lives on the subject phase’s own chip while the others are deliberately blanked. The verdict now reads the whole capsule, matching the suite. t8 is a genuine, documented divergence: its line describes the run and its footnote describes the opened phase. That is reported as `sentenceRowFollowsOpenPhase` and deliberately kept OUT of the exit gate, so it stays visible without being failed.

still_open.summary: The append-only arrival path still never engages on the windowed thread.
still_open.detail: data.visibleSlice recomputes its start from the message count, so on thread-09 (700 messages, window 50) an append also drops the oldest rendered message. That is a removal, and the append gate correctly refuses it. Unchanged this pass; fixing it means changing visibleSlice/loadedFrom semantics in shared/data.js.
